text: According to the Representational Theory of Mind (RTM), mental processes are best understood as:
choices: Direct sensorimotor engagement with environmental affordances that bypasses any inner states
Dispositions to behave, with no internal states that stand for anything
Causal processes operating over internal representations that carry content
Processes describable only by differential equations, never in terms of content
explanation: RTM holds that cognition consists in causal processes defined over internal representations that carry content (states that are 'about' things). Option 1 is the enactivist/Gibsonian view and option 2 is behaviourism, both of which deny contentful inner states; the last option describes the dynamical-systems (van Gelder) alternative that tries to explain cognition without representations. Only the third option states RTM's core commitment.
